newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: New country fund shakes up Mauritius bourse.
newsitem.headline: New country fund shakes up Mauritius bourse.

text.p: The Mauritius bourse index Semdex rose by 4.68 points on Friday to 310.09, stimulated by news that a new country fund had been set up with investments to focus on state-linked enterprises and the Mauritian bourse.
Volume surged to 10.42 million rupees on 434,344 shares from 5.23 million rupees on 153,911 shares on Wednesday.

A Thursday announcement by Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam setting up a new $60 million Port Louis Fund Ltd as a so-called country fund was responsible for an end to a fall that lasted 19 consecutive trading sessions, brokers said.
The last time Semdex made gains was on September 9.

Port Louis Fund Ltd will invest $45 million in equities of state-linked companies such as Air Mauritius, State Bank of Mauritius, Mauritius Telecom and the State Investment Corporation, according to offficial documents.
The remaining $15 million has been earmarked for investments in the Stock Exchange of Mauritius and other unquoted, high performing companies, the documents showed.
"We cannot expect hearing (about) $15 million coming on the market everyday...It is the first true good economic news of this government," one broker said.
The broker said buying was also bolstered by attractive share prices as the recent depressed market drove most stocks to undervalued levels.

"Since the market was pretty much undervalued, it will not surprise us if this upsurge goes on for a while. We hope the prime minister has other good news for us with the upcoming government reshuffle," the broker added.
Ramgoolam, who was elected prime minister last December, promised a cabinet reshuffle in early August when Finance Minister Rundheersing Bheenick resigned.
Mauritius Commercial Bank gained one rupee to 71 on 20,695 shares while State Bank of Mauritius rose 10 cents to 8.60. British American Insurance rose 20 cents to 7.20 rupees on 27,326 shares.
